hypothesis: Reducing the large-input grid cap from 1024 to 256 limits output atomics to at most 256 per call while preserving one input pass and the per-call reset. This may reduce contention, but it may also reduce memory-level parallelism; the controller should compare total time including reset and launch overhead and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
notes: This is a cap-only contrast to the selected parent; correctness and performance for the candidate have not been measured.
transformations: Keep the asynchronous per-call output reset and the one-pass input reduction with one CTA atomicAdd.
Reduce the large-input grid cap from 1024 CTAs to 256; retain ceil(n/256) blocks for smaller inputs.
